main_text.p: offerimus,etiam atque etiam obsecran-tes, vt Christianissimum vestrum fasti[?]-gium, quàm diutissimè Orbi tueatur incolume. Rogamus proinde domi-nationem vestram, vt & illos, Cyrillum scilicet & Memnone, & nos quoq; (om-nes enim vinctis vtpote Fratribꝰ sacraeq; Synodi Præsidibus colligati sumus) à vinculis tãdem absoluat.] Postremò,vt abunde omnibus satisfiat, ipsum audia-mus Cyrillum in suâ Apologiâ ad Impera-torem, ita sub mitè & modestè suppli-cantem: [Decet itaq; excellentes præ-stantésq; naturas, vt sereno placidóque sint animo: hæc autem lenitas animiq; serenitas, singulari modo adest diuinæ supremæq; illi naturæ, q̃ vestra Maje-stas pro viribꝰ imitans quandam quoq; huius clementiæ imaginem videtur prę se ferre. Siquidem terrenum illud Re-gnum, cœlestis illius quoddam simula-chrum, & quasi vmbra quædam inter homines iudicatur,vos itaq; soli in om-nes Imperiū sortiti, timore ac mansue-tudine subditos vestros in officio conti-netis,& veluti illustrem quandam paca-támq; prosperitatem p vniuersum Or-bem

page.notes: The facing page on the right is cut off by the scan edge; only the first letters of its lines are visible, so its fragments are given as far as they can be read. Doubtful readings: "fasti[?]" (the word is broken by a damaged glyph in the scan). "Fratribꝰ" is printed with a superscript ꝰ. Long s has been written as s throughout. Italic passages are marked with <i>. The text runs on from the previous page and ends with "Or-bem" at the foot of the column.
